evidence.claim: Pending candidates are materialized, evaluated, gated and persisted before merge-group finalization.
Groups wait for pending evaluations then create child branch for accepted candidate, not hot-activate current harness.
Hook menu covers prompts, subagents, tools, middleware and runtime controls; one virtual hook change required.
Candidate files are bounded to declared safe relative surfaces and changed values recorded.
Accept when no split mean pass rate decreases and at least one improves; default train/heldout and two repeats.
Validate repeat cardinality/uniqueness and passed/total ranges, and compare repeat denominators.
Backend executes task-environment commands asynchronously with timeout result 124; timeout of await is not proof remote process died.
Authored loop holds weights/evaluator fixed while proposing bounded harness edits and promoting candidates.

strengths: Harness edit surfaces include runtime/tool policy, with evaluation and promotion recorded separately.
Per-split acceptance prevents aggregate gain from hiding a mean drop in one split.
limits: Mean pass-rate gain with two default repeats is not statistical confidence or proof of task identity equality.
Promotion to branch records does not establish safe in-place activation, shared-service boundary or native rebuild continuity.
arconaut_questions: Which mutable programs are candidate surfaces, and which independent invariant oracles survive their replacement?
How should model-governed experiment selection expose uncertainty and generalization while permitting operator steering?
